label: C-02
title: Antimatter has no kill switch of its own; every way to halt annihilation belongs to a different principal
fingerprintNote: sha256(contract:function:rootCauseClass)[:16] - legacy form, empty entryPoint. Carried verbatim from sanitized.json; reproduces from fingerprintBasis.

classification.assetImpact: No direct impact. Incident-response capability only: if a defect is found in Antimatter itself - including H-01 - its own owner cannot stop it. The fastest available lever (FlaxToken.revokeAllMintPrivileges) is global and silently de-authorises PhusdStableMinter too.
attackPath: 1. A live defect in annihilateFrom is discovered.
2. Antimatter is not Pausable and exposes no owner lever to halt annihilation.
3. Halting requires PhusdStableMinter's pauser/owner, FlaxToken's owner, or the yield strategy's owner - all principals independent of Antimatter.owner().
4. The only fast lever is global and causes collateral damage.
classification.likelihood: Conditional on another defect existing - which H-01 demonstrates is not hypothetical.
classification.assumptions: The independent owners are not the same party, which nothing enforces.

justification: Centralization/governance-structure finding, C-02 at QA severity. It causes nothing on its own and is therefore not Medium; it is worth reporting because it is a severity MULTIPLIER on every other finding here - H-01 is a one-transaction theft that Antimatter's own owner has no proportionate lever to stop. Filed as a runbook-or-pause-flag recommendation, not as an owner-trust complaint.
recommendation: Either document the incident-response runbook (who to call, in what order) or add an owner-settable `annihilationPaused` flag checked at the top of annihilateFrom, so the contract's own owner holds a proportionate, non-global lever.

sanitizer.reason: No known-issues document exists for this project (knownIssuesFile/Source null, knownIssues empty, verified at HEAD) so KI suppression has no authority; no C4 known-invalid class genuinely applies; not a malicious-owner vector; ledger empty so no prior entry to reconcile against.

additionalContext.rootCause: Antimatter is not Pausable and exposes no owner lever to stop annihilation. Halting requires PhusdStableMinter's pauser or owner, FlaxToken's owner, or the yield strategy's owner - all principals independent of Antimatter.owner(), with nothing requiring them to be the same party.
additionalContext.impact: If a defect is found in Antimatter itself - including DEDUP-001 - its own owner cannot stop it, and the fastest lever (FlaxToken.revokeAllMintPrivileges) is global: it silently de-authorises PhusdStableMinter too.
additionalContext.law3Note: This is an operational observation, NOT a 'malicious owner' finding: no owner needs to misbehave for the incident-response path to be missing.
additionalContext.whyQa: The composition is arguably deliberate (Antimatter keeps no stablecoin list and defers control to the minter), and a rushed pause would itself add attack surface.

mergeAction: Kept separate from DEDUP-011 - see that entry's mergeAction for the verification and rationale.
